newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices seen mostly steady in thin talk.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices seen mostly steady in thin talk.

text.p: Wholesale power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were reported to be relatively steady in thin discussion Monday with little demand due to mild weather, industry sources said.

Texas Utilities 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear unit 1 resumed power output over the weekend after a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage . The unit was operating at 28 percent of capacity as of early Monday and was expected to reach full power near Thursday.
Temperatures through much of Texas were forecast to reach highs in the mid 70s degrees Fahrenheit Monday, and reach up into the mid-80s degrees Fahrenheit in south Texas Tuesday.
Prices for peak, firm power for Tuesday delivery were talked steady at $25.25-26.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
However, some Tuesday peak power was quoted above and below that range, with one unconfirmed 16-hour ERCOT deal reported at $22.75 and some talk of offers as high as $29.00 per MWh.
Off-peak non-firm ERCOT power transactions for Tuesday were said to be non-existant, with notional quotes in the $10.00-12.00 per MWh range.
December peak power was talked steady at $25.25-25.75, while January/February ERCOT power prices were assessed unchanged at $25.30-25.85, the sources said.
